messages:
maria: fyi - nightly CI bench started spitting inconsistent kernel-selection numbers overnight. noticed jump in p50 latency for the small-seq workload.
liam: saw that alert. which job? nightly-replay-smallseq?
maria: yes. bench-bot posted the run: https://ci.internal/redwood/bench/1788002
shreya: grabbing the logs now. quick glance: kselect fallback to generic kernel at 01:12:07 UTC multiple times.
devon: that usually happens when a kernel probe fails — could be a cuda driver hiccup or the selector threshold misfire.
anya: stack: selector v2.4.1, kernel-cache TTL 5m, batching heuristic = dynamic-window (target 8ms).
bench-bot: [run-summary] model: redwood-small-v1, seq=128, batch-policy=dynamic-window, runs=20, median-p50=18.9ms, median-p95=46.2ms, flaky-runs=3
maria: here's the noisy snippet from the profiler:
```
2026-11-02T01:11:58Z selector: picked kernel fast_gemm_fp16
2026-11-02T01:12:07Z selector: kernel probe failed (nvrtc timeout)
2026-11-02T01:12:07Z selector: fallback -> generic_gemm
2026-11-02T01:12:07Z runtime: kv-cache hitrate drop 93% -> 60%
2026-11-02T01:12:14Z latency spike +120%
```
liam: kv-cache drop looks suspicious — maybe cache eviction during fallback? does the selector change layout or stream that invalidates the cache?
shreya: selector change can remap kernels onto different CUDA streams. if we rebind tensors we might invalidate device pointers used by our KV cache wrapper.
devon: ok plausible. two remediation options: 1) make selector avoid stream remap on warm paths, 2) make KV cache robust to pointer aliasing. both need careful perf tests.
anya: also want to rule out infra flakiness. ci-bot, any node reboots or driver updates around that time?
ci-bot: [system-note] no orchestrator node restarts recorded between 2026-11-02T01:00:00 and 2026-11-02T02:00:00. GPU driver version unchanged on pool-gpu-12.
maria: good. next: we need an apples-to-apples CI job that intentionally toggles selector behavior and measures KV hit consistency across kernels.
liam: propose new job: bench/selector-stability with 3 arms: (A) pinned kernel selection, (B) dynamic selection but no stream remap, (C) dynamic selection with remap. each arm run 100 iterations across seq distribution.
shreya: also add deterministic replay harness input (same traffic seed) and a small synthetic tail distribution to exercise evictions.
devon: add a guarded assertion in the harness to check KV cache addresses between iterations. if pointer changes, emit a trace event.
anya: example CI snippet:
```
jobs:
  selector-stability:
    runs-on: gpu
    matrix:
      arm: [pinned, dyn-no-remap, dyn-remap]
    steps:
      - run: ./bench/run_selector_stability --iterations=100 --seed=42 --emit-trace
```
maria: target landing plan:
- spike job in nightly for 3 days
- publish dashboard widget: kernel selection breakdown + kv-cache hit rate time series
- add alert: >5% runs with kernel fallback or kv hitrate drop >15% over median
liam: for flaky triage: tag runs with run-id, store traces in s3://bench-traces/selector-stability/<run-id>. CI should mark runs as flaky if result variance >10% p50 across repeats.
shreya: I'll open a PR with the job + harness changes. will also include a small flamegraph snapshot upload step.
devon: I'll prototype a KV-cache pointer-stability guard and test locally on devbox.
anya: want metric names: selector.fallback.count, selector.kernel.name, kvcache.hitrate, bench.latency.p50, bench.latency.p95
maria: perfect. once PR is up, bench-bot can run a canary and post initial numbers to this thread.
bench-bot: ack - will run canary on merge and post run-summary + trace links. :gear:
maria: thanks everyone. aim to get PR reviews + canary by EOD. if we still see flakiness after fixes we'll expand to dedicated ci pool to see infra influence.
